selection.reason: D1015 supplied the previously missing finite and locally-finite paracompact closed-cover comparison. Combining that comparison, the existing open-cover comparison, and the existing free-index invariant-cochain calculation now gives the exact p.210 canonical isomorphism without another live TeX statement.

derivation.fixed_point_free_meaning: The index G-set is free, exactly the hypothesis of the free-index lemma.
derivation.open_case: The open acyclic-cover lemma identifies derived equivariant Cech cohomology with H^n(X;G,A); the free-index lemma identifies the former with H^n(C(U,A)^G).
derivation.closed_paracompact_case: The closed acyclic-cover lemma applies to a locally finite closed G-covering on a paracompact X; the free-index lemma applies to its nonalternating coefficient complex.
derivation.finite_case: In context this is the finite alternative inside the closed-cover branch inherited from Corollary 2 to Theorem 5.5.3. The finite branch of the closed acyclic-cover lemma and the free-index lemma give the same canonical isomorphism.
derivation.canonical_isomorphism: The canonical free-index comparison followed by the canonical acyclic-cover edge map is an isomorphism H^n(C(U,A)^G) to H^n(X;G,A); its inverse is the source's displayed canonical isomorphism.
derivation.excluded_reading: No assertion is made for an arbitrary finite covering by subsets that are neither open nor closed.

mapping_projection.rationale: Stacks now proves the complete source corollary. The open-cover acyclic comparison and the new closed-cover acyclic comparison cover respectively the open branch and the finite/locally-finite paracompact closed branches, while the fixed-point-free index lemma identifies derived invariants of the nonalternating Cech complex with the cohomology of its invariant subcomplex.
